spots.name: Shah Mosque
spots.summary: The Shah Mosque, also officially known as the Imam Mosque or Imam Khomeini Mosque, is a mosque located on the south side of Naqsh-e Jahan Square in Isfahan, in the province of Isfahan, Iran. Its construction began in 1611, during the Safavid Empire under the order of Abbas the Great, and was completed c. 1630.

spots.name: Naqsh-e Jahan Square
spots.summary: The Naqsh-e Jahan Square, also known as the Shah Square prior to 1979, and sometimes known as the Imam Square, is a square situated at the center of Isfahan, Iran. Constructed between 1598 and 1629, it is now an important historical site, and one of UNESCO's World Heritage Sites.

spots.name: Jameh Mosque of Isfahan

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Jāmeh Mosque of Isfahān or Jāme' Mosque of Isfahān, also known as the Atiq Mosque and the Friday Mosque of Isfahān, is a historic congregational mosque (Jāmeh), located in Isfahan, Iran. The mosque is the result of continual construction, reconstruction, additions and renovations on the site from c.

spots.name: Sheikh Lotfollah Mosque
spots.summary: The Sheikh Lotfollah Mosque is a Shi'ite mosque, located on the eastern side of Naqsh-e Jahan Square, Isfahan, Iran. Construction of the mosque started in 1011 AH (1602/1603 CE) and was finished in 1028 AH (1618/1619 CE). It is one of the masterpieces of Iranian architecture from the Safavid era.

spots.name: Chehel Sotoun
spots.summary: Chehel Sotoun is a 17th century pavilion and garden, in Isfahan, Iran. It was commissioned by Abbas the Great and completed by Shah Abbas II, both Safavid Shahs, mostly for royal entertainment and receptions.

spots.name: Si-o-se-pol
spots.summary: The Allahverdi Khan Bridge, popularly known as Si-o-se-pol, is the largest of the eleven historical bridges on the Zayanderud, the largest river of the Iranian Plateau, in Isfahan, Iran.

spots.name: Vank Cathedral
spots.summary: The Holy Savior Cathedral, also known the Church of the Saintly Sisters, is an Armenian Apostolic cathedral located in the New Julfa district of Isfahan, Iran. It is commonly referred to as the Vank, which means "monastery" or "convent" in the Armenian language.

spots.name: Ali Qapu

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Ali Qapu is an imperial palace in Isfahan, Iran. It is located on the western side of Naqsh-e Jahan Square, opposite to Sheikh Lotfollah Mosque, and had originally been designed as a vast portal entrance to the grand palace which stretched from the square to Chaharbagh Boulevard.

spots.name: Khaju Bridge
spots.summary: The Khaju Bridge is a historic bridge on the Zayanderud, the largest river of the Iranian plateau, in Isfahan, Iran. Serving as both a bridge and a weir, it links the Khaju quarter on the north bank with the Zoroastrian quarter across the Zayanderud. It is located at the end of Kamal Ismail Street in Isfahan.

spots.name: Hasht Behesht
spots.summary: Hasht Behesht or Hasht-Behesht is a 17th-century pavilion in Isfahan, Iran. It was built by the order of Suleiman I, the eighth shah of Safavid Iran, and functioned mainly as a private pavilion. It is located in Isfahan's famous Charbagh Street. It was also the first modern school in Isfahan called His Majesty's School.

spots.name: Monar Jonban
spots.summary: The Menar Jonban, is a mosque and mausoleum, located in Esfahan, in the province of Isfahan, Iran.

spots.name: Chaharbagh School

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Chahār Bāgh School or the Chahār Bāgh Madrasa, also known as Madrese-ye Madar-e Shah, is a 17–18th century cultural complex in Isfahan, Iran. The compound was built in the late Safavid era, during the reign of Shah Soltan Hoseyn, to serve as a theological and clerical school.

spots.name: Chaharbagh
spots.summary: Chahar Bagh Boulevard is a historic avenue in Isfahan constructed during the Safavid era. This historic street is very similar to the Champs-Élysées in Paris. Therefore, some visitors have called it the Champs-Élysées of Isfahan.

spots.name: Flower Garden of Isfahan
spots.summary: The Flower garden of Isfahan was a major green space project completed in the 1990s in Isfahan, Iran. Serving multiple purposes, the garden is a recreational, cultural, educational and research center. Its buildings incorporate traditional Iranian elements.

spots.name: Natural History Museum of Isfahan

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Natural History Museum of Isfahan, Iran, is located in a building that dates from the 15th century Timurid era. The building includes large halls and a veranda which are decorated by muqarnas and stucco. This building became a museum in 1988.

spots.name: Hakim Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Hakim Mosque is a Shi'ite mosque, located in Esfahan, in the province of Isfahan, Iran. The mosque is located adjacent to the Isfahan Bazaar. The mosque also serves as a public building, as a madrasa, as a community center for functions, and an emergency shelter for travellers.

spots.name: Bedkhem Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Holy Bethlehem Church of New Julfa, also Bedkhem Church, is an Armenian Apostolic church in the New Julfa quarter in Isfahan, Iran. One of the most important historical churches of the city, it belongs to the Abbas I era. The church is located in the Julfa square near Saint Mary Church.

spots.name: Darb-e Imam

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Darb-e Imam is a Twelver Shi'ite Imamzadeh complex located in the Dardasht quarter of Esfahan, in the province of Isfahan, Iran. The complex comprises two shrines, a mosque, a mausoleum, and a royal cemetery.

spots.name: Rashk-e Jenan

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Isfahan Governor's Palace resides within the walls of the Rashk-e Jenan, also known as Rashk Palace. The building was built in the Safavid era, in Isfahan, Darvazeh Dowlat, on Bagh-e Goldasteh Street. It's listed in Iran's National Heritage list since 16 March 1986, under the registration number 1710.

spots.name: Ali Gholi Agha hammam
spots.summary: The Ali Gholi Agha hammam is a historic hammam in the Bidabad district of Isfahan, Iran. The hammam was built in 1713 by Ali Gholi Agha, who was a courtier of the Safavid shahs Suleiman I and Soltan Hoseyn. Its architectural style is Isfahani and it was built in the late Safavid era.

spots.name: Ali minaret

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Ali minaret, constructed in the 11th century, is the oldest minaret in Isfahan, Iran. It is close to the Ali mosque. This minaret is 52 metres (171 ft) in height and is the second highest historical minaret in Isfahan after the Sarban minaret.

spots.name: Takht-e Foulad
spots.summary: The Takht-e Foulad, also known as Lissanul Arz, is a historical, predominately Islamic, cemetery located in Esfahan, in the province of Isfahan, Iran. It is a large funerary complex that includes several historic mausoleums, mosques, tekyehs, sub-cemeteries and standalone graves.

spots.name: Chehel Dokhtaran minaret

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Chehel Dokhtaran minaret is a historical minaret in Isfahan, Iran. It is located in the Jouybareh district of Isfahan. According to the kufic inscription on the minaret, it is built in 1112. It is the fifth oldest minaret in Iran, which has an inscription. There's a big window on the minaret, which faces the qibla.

spots.name: Seyyed Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Seyyed Mosque is a Twelver Shi'ite mosque and madrasa, located in Isfahan, Isfahan province, Iran. It was built in the late 19th century, during the Qajar era, by the Shi'ite cleric Mohammad Bagher Shafti, one of the first clerics to receive the rank of Hujjatul Islam.

spots.name: Saeb Mausoleum
spots.summary: The Saeb Mausoleum is an Islamic mausoleum, located in Isfahan, Isfahan province, Iran. The mausoleum is the burial place of Mohammad Ali ibn Mirza Abdul Rahim Tabrizi, more commonly known as Saib Tabrizi, a famous 17th century Iranian poet.

spots.name: Qeysarie Gate
spots.summary: The Qeysarie gate is a historic gate in the main entrance of the Grand Bazaar of Isfahan in Isfahan, Iran. The gate originally had 3 floors, but the third floor was destroyed later. The destroyed third floor had been a Naqqarekhane. The gate was built in the 17th century during the Safavid era

spots.name: Imamzadeh Ismail

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Imamzadeh Ismail and Shayah Mosque is a Twelver Shia imamzadeh, mausoleum, and mosque complex, located in Esfahan, in the province of Isfahan, Iran, which dates from both the Seljuk and Safavid periods.

spots.name: Shahrestan Bridge
spots.summary: The Shahrestan bridge is the oldest bridge on the Zayandeh River in Iran. The foundations date back to the Sasanian era, but the top was renovated twice, first in the 10th century by the Buyids, then in the 11th century during the Seljuk era.

spots.name: Imamzadeh Haroun-e-Velayat

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Imamzadeh Haroun-e-Velayat, also known as the Harun-i Vilayat Mausoleum, is a Shia imamzadeh, mausoleum, and madrasa complex, located in the city of Esfahan, in the province of Isfahan, Iran.

spots.name: St. Mary Church, Isfahan

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Saint Mary Church of New Julfa is a historical Armenian church in Isfahan, Iran, completed in 1613.

spots.name: Sarban minaret

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Sarban minaret is a historic Seljuk era minaret in Isfahan, Iran. The Sarban minaret is located in the north of Jouybareh district, not far from Chehel Dokhtaran minaret. It seems that there was a mosque beside this minaret in the past, but it does not exist any more. The minaret consists of seven different parts.

spots.name: Museum of Contemporary Art, Isfahan

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Museum of Contemporary Art is a contemporary art museum in Isfahan, Iran, located next to the Museum of Natural History. The museum is housed in the Chaharbagh Palace, originally built in 17th century under Safavid rule.

spots.name: Kohneh Square
spots.summary: Kohneh Square is a city square which has been active for centuries in the city of Isfahan, Iran, serving cultural, religious and economic functions. It was once the city's main square. The complex is located near the Grand Bazaar, and the Jameh Mosque.

spots.name: Nazhvan Forest Park
spots.summary: The Nazhvan Forest Park is one of the few gardens in Isfahan, which has been rather safe from expansion and development of the city and freshens the air of Isfahan. The word nazhvan consists of two words nazh, which means "poplar" in Persian and van, which is a Persian suffix for place.

spots.name: Tohidkhaneh

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Tohidkhaneh is a historical building in Isfahan, Iran. The building is located behind the Ālī Qāpū palace. It was used as the kitchen and the prison of the palace for some time. It is said that Sufis met there on Friday evenings in the era of Abbas I, during which they prayed for the Shah.

spots.name: Imamzadeh Ahmad

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Imamzadeh Ahmad is a Shi'ite imamzadeh in Isfahan, Iran. The Imamzadeh comprises a mausoleum, to the north and west of which are two iwans; the tomb faces a vast sahn where several famous people, like Amir Kabir's daughter and Naser al-Din Shah's sister, are buried.

spots.name: Baba Ghassem Mausoleum
spots.summary: The Baba Ghassem Mausoleum, also known as the Baba Qasem Mausoleum, is a mausoleum in the Ebn-e Sina district of the city of Esfahan, in the province of Isfahan, Iran. The building was completed in 1431 CE, during the Ilkhanid era; and is located to the north of Jameh Mosque of Isfahan.

spots.name: Setti Fatemeh Mausoleum

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Mausoleum of Safavid Princes, also known as the Mausoleum of Seti Fatemeh, is Twelver Shi'ite mausoleum and funerary complex, located in the Chaharsu-ye-Kuchak district of Isfahan, Iran.

spots.name: Darozziafe minarets

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Darozziafe minarets are two historical minarets in Isfahan, Iran. The minarets are located in the old Jouybareh district on the Ebn-e-Sina street. These 14th century minarets are built on both sides of a portal. There is an inscription with white script on the ultramarine background under the above muqarnas.

spots.name: Museum of Decorative Arts, Isfahan

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The museum of decorative arts in Isfahan was founded in 1995. More than 3000 artworks from the Safavid and Qajar eras are kept in the museum.

spots.name: Joubi Bridge
spots.summary: Joubi Bridge, also called the Choobi Bridge, is a bridge over the Zayanderud in Isfahan, Iran. It was built in 1655, during the Safavid era.

spots.name: Shahshahan Mausoleum

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Shahshahan Mausoleum, officially known as the Buq'ah-i Shah 'Ala al-Din Muhammad, is a mausoleum and hussainiya, located in the Ebn-e Sina district of Isfahan, Isfahan province, Iran. The mausoleum contains the tomb of Shah Ala al-Din Muhammad, or known simply as Shah Alaeddin.

spots.name: Roknolmolk Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Roknolmolk Mosque, formerly known as the Aksa Mosque, is a Twelver Shi'ite mosque, located in Esfahan, in the province of Isfahan, Iran. Completed in the early part of the 20th century, the mosque was built during the Qajar era and is situated adjacent to the Takht-e Foulad cemetery.

spots.name: Jarchi hammam
spots.summary: The Jarchi hammam or Jarchibashi hammam is a historic structure in Isfahan, Iran. The hammam belongs to the Safavid era. It is located in the Hakim street.

spots.name: Khosro Agha hammam
spots.summary: The Khosro Agha hammam was a historical hammam in Iran. It was located in Sepah street in Isfahan and belonged to the Safavid era.

spots.name: Nimavar school
spots.summary: Nimavar School is a historical school in Isfahan, Iran. It's located in Nimavar Bazaar and belongs to Safavid era. This school was built in 1691 in the era of Suleiman I.

spots.name: Mausoleum of Baba Rokneddin

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Mausoleum of Baba Rukn al-Din, or simply known as the Mausoleum of Baba Rokneddin, is a mausoleum located within the grounds of the Takht-e Foulad cemetery in the city of Esfahan, in the province of Isfahan, Iran.

spots.name: Mesri Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Mesri Mosque is a Shi'ite mosque, located in Esfahan, in the province of Isfahan, Iran. The mosque was built in 1061 AH (1650/1651 CE), during the Safavid era. In the mihrab there is an inscription in Nastaliq script, written by Mohammad Reza Emami, a calligrapher.

spots.name: Soltan Bakht Agha Mausoleum
spots.summary: The Soltan Bakht Agha Mausoleum is a mausoleum located in the city of Esfahan, in the province of Isfahan, Iran. The mausoleum complex entombs the remains of Soltan Bakht Agha, the niece of the Injuid ruler, Abu Ishaq Inju.

spots.name: Dardasht minarets

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Soltan Bakht Agha Mausoleum is a mausoleum located in the city of Esfahan, in the province of Isfahan, Iran. The mausoleum complex entombs the remains of Soltan Bakht Agha, the niece of the Injuid ruler, Abu Ishaq Inju.

spots.name: St. Jacob Church, New Julfa

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Saint Jacob of Nisibis Church of New Julfa,, is an Armenian Apostolic church in New Julfa, Iran. It is located inside St. Mary Church and is considered the oldest surviving church in New Julfa.

spots.name: Asarkhane Shahi
spots.summary: Asarkhane Shahi is a Safavid era oil mill constructed during the reign of Shah Abbas I at the same time as the Grand bazaar of Isfahan and Molla Abdollah School. The main area of the Asarkhane Shahi was about 1,800 square, but now it is 380 square meters.

spots.name: Enqelab Square
spots.summary: Enqelab Square is a square in downtown Isfahan, Iran. It is located between the southern tip of Chahar Bagh Boulevard and the historical Si-o-se-pol bridge. Si-o-se Pol Metro Station is just across the bridge.

spots.name: St. Gregory the Illuminator Church, New Julfa

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Saint Gregory the Illuminator Church of New Julfa,, is an Armenian Apostolic church in New Julfa, Iran. It is located in Small Meidan neighbourhood of New Julfa.
spots.wikipediaTitle: St. Gregory the Illuminator Church, New Julfa

spots.name: Kassegaran Madrasa
spots.summary: Kassegaran Madrasa is a historical madrasa in Isfahan, Iran. It belongs to the era of the Safavid King Suleiman. According to the thuluth inscription above its portal, it was built in 1694 by the order and under supervision of Amir Mohammad Mehdi Hakimolmolk Ardestani.

spots.name: Isfahan Central Library and Information Center

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Isfahan Central Library and Information Center is a library in the Iranian city of Isfahan. It is 12,000 square metres (130,000 sq ft), and houses 130,000 books.
